weekly_summary:
**Week of May 20, 2026**

Okay so this week had a real "let's get practical" energy and I'm here for it. Dr. Tony Hampton dropped a video called "Why I Stopped Telling People To Buy Ribeye" and honestly? The comments section was more inspiring than the video itself. One guy shared he's lost 90 lbs eating mostly 80/20 ground beef, pork chops, eggs, and pickles, and his grocery bill actually went *down* from when he was buying processed stuff. Ten months in with his wife and they're crushing it. That's the kind of real-world carnivore that doesn't get enough airtime, you know?

I think there's been this weird pressure in the community to make everything look Instagram-perfect with fancy cuts and elaborate meal prep, but the truth is most of us are just trying to make this sustainable without going broke. Ground beef is the unsung hero. Eggs are clutch. You don't need a tomahawk steak to heal your metabolism. It's giving "do what works for YOUR life" and I love that we're finally saying it out loud more.

It's got me thinking, what's the one "unglamorous" staple that's actually carrying your carnivore journey right now? Mine's definitely canned sardines, judge me if you want. 🐟

# Marcus's Analysis: Week of May 13-20, 2026

## The Big Picture

What's jumping out at me this week is a clear shift in the carnivore conversation, we're moving away from the "ribeye lifestyle" messaging toward practical, budget-conscious approaches. Dr. Tony Hampton's video "Why I Stopped Telling People To Buy Ribeye" pulling 21,598 views with exceptional engagement tells me something important is happening in our community.

## Key Insight #1: The Affordability Revolution

**What I'm seeing:** That top comment with 134 likes is doing more persuasion work than most content creators realize. Robert Wilhelm sharing his 90-lb loss eating primarily 80/20 ground beef, with ribeyes only once weekly, is the exact proof point newcomers need.

**Why this matters:** The #1 objection I hear is "carnivore is too expensive." This content directly demolishes that barrier.

**Actionable takeaway:** If you're creating content or coaching people, lead with ground beef, eggs, and pork chops. Save the ribeye talk for optimization conversations later. The Wilhelms actually *reduced* their grocery bill going carnivore, that's the story that converts skeptics.

## Key Insight #2: The "Boring Works" Protocol

**Specific example:** Look at Robert's daily template, 1 lb ground beef, 6 eggs, sardines. That's maybe $8-12/day depending on location. Simple, repeatable, effective.

**The pattern:** 10 months consistent, 90 lbs down. No fancy protocols, no exotic meats.

**For practitioners:** Stop overcomplicating this. A rotation of ground beef, eggs, pork chops, and occasional steaks is a complete framework.

## What I'd Watch Next Week

The engagement ratio on this video (2,249 likes, 278 comments on 21.5K views) is unusually high, over 10% engagement. Budget carnivore content is resonating hard right now.
